questions.question: How does a muscle move a bone?
questions.expected_answer: A muscle is joined to a bone by a tendon. When the muscle contracts, it gets shorter and fatter and pulls on the bone, so the bone moves at a joint. Muscles can only pull, never push.

questions.question: Explain how the biceps and triceps work together to bend and straighten the arm.
questions.expected_answer: They are a pair. To bend the arm, the biceps contracts and pulls the forearm up while the triceps relaxes. To straighten it, the triceps contracts and pulls the forearm down while the biceps relaxes.

questions.question: Why do we need joints to move? Name one hinge joint and one ball and socket joint.
questions.expected_answer: Bones can only move where they meet at a joint; without joints the skeleton would be one stiff piece. Hinge joints include the knee and elbow. Ball and socket joints include the shoulder and hip.
